div.head: Cons Cn II 19.2a
div.ab: [Teoþunga. Sicut regnum diuiditur in plures comitatus, comitatus in plura centenaria, ita centenarium unum in plures decimationes, sicut centum unum in plures decarios numeros.
div.note: New row (October 2026): Liebermann’s text transcribed from Gesetze I p. 618 (two independent readings of the page images, differences settled against the page)

note.seg: 19, 2a—d nur in Hk, verfasst im 12. Jh., vielleicht in Kent und (laut Sprachgebrauchs: centenarium, decimatio) wohl vom Autor der Consil., aber, da Hr fehlend, erst nachträglich. Vgl. über diese Glosse Palgrave Rise II p. cxxv; Waitz Deutsche Verf. I 448

19, 2a—d only in Hk, composed in the 12th cent., perhaps in Kent and (to judge by the usage: centenarium, decimatio) probably by the author of the Consil., but, since missing in Hr, only subsequently. On this gloss cf. Palgrave Rise II p. cxxv; Waitz Deutsche Verf. I 448
Teodunga, neben d steht uel þ Hk
Teodunga, with uel þ beside the d, Hk
Vgl. Gl Zehnerschaft 1. g. 22. 26c. 27a. b; Grafschaft 4a. 7; Hundred 13c; Eideshelfer 13, wo dies nachzutragen
Cf. Gl Zehnerschaft 1. g. 22. 26c. 27a. b; Grafschaft 4a. 7; Hundred 13c; Eideshelfer 13, where this should be added
